cards.text: At that time, Abimelech, king of Gerar (Genesis 20:2), comes to Abraham with Phicol, the commander of his army. A king AND his army commander, together? Friend, when two bosses walk up to your desk at the same time, you check your pulse.

cards.question: Abimelech opens with something he's noticed about Abraham. What does he say?

answers.text: God is with him in all he does
His flocks grow bigger every year

cards.text: Then Abimelech gets to the point. He wants Abraham to swear an oath, right there before God.

cards.question: What does Abimelech want Abraham to swear before God?

answers.text: He won't deal falsely with him or his family
He will give the king half of his flocks
He will leave the king's land by spring

cards.question: Abimelech also asks Abraham to show him and the country the same kindness Abimelech has shown Abraham.
Abraham tells Abimelech he needs time to think it over before he swears anything.

cards.text: Abraham says, “I swear it.” Two words, done. But then Abraham's got a complaint of his own, and he takes it straight to the king.

cards.question: What is Abraham's complaint to Abimelech about?

answers.text: A well the king's servants seized
Sheep stolen out of his flock
A field the king's army burned

cards.question: Abimelech says he knew all about the well and was waiting for Abraham to bring it up.

cards.text: Abimelech says he has no idea who did it, and since Abraham never told him, today's the first he's hearing of it. Friend, that's me in every group chat: "Wait. WHEN did this happen?"

cards.question: So Abraham brings Abimelech ___ and ___, and the two men make a covenant.

cards.text: Covenant made. Then Abraham separates some ewe lambs from the flock and sets them off by themselves, and I bet Abimelech's standing there like, "Uh. What are THOSE for?"

cards.question: Abraham sets apart ___ ewe lambs from the flock.
Abimelech asks Abraham why he set those lambs apart. What does Abraham say the lambs are?

answers.text: His witness that he dug the well
A gift for the king's children
An offering for a safe journey

cards.question: That place ends up with a name: Beersheba. Why does it get that name?

answers.text: The two men swore an oath there

cards.text: With the covenant made, Abimelech and Phicol get up and head back to the land of the Philistines. Abraham's still in Beersheba, and he's not done there yet.

cards.question: Abraham plants a ___ tree in Beersheba.
There in Beersheba, what else does Abraham do?

answers.text: He calls on the name of the LORD
He builds a house for Sarah
He digs a second well nearby

cards.question: Abraham stays in the land of the Philistines for a long time.

cards.text: Abraham calls on the LORD, the Eternal God, and settles in for a long stay. That's where we leave him for now, friend, but trust me, Abraham's story has plenty of oven time left.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says "Two words, done" about "I swear it," which is three words. The point he makes isn't true.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: Either right answer fits either blank. Genesis 21:27 lists "sheep and cattle," but "So Abraham brings Abimelech cattle and sheep" means the same thing. The card ties sheep to blank 1 and cattle to blank 2, so a baker who swaps them could be marked wrong for a reading that is accurate.
findings.question: When the two right answers in a two-blank fill in the blank could go in either blank, should both orders count as right, or should cards like this be rewritten so each blank has only one possible answer?

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess a number (seven) that nothing earlier sets up and that can't be reasoned out. It tests a detail the baker hasn't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question says "those lambs," which points back to cards 12 and 13. Those cards are no longer on screen. The question should name the seven ewe lambs.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question opens with "That place" and never says which place: where Abraham and Abimelech made their covenant over the well.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the kind of tree (tamarisk). That is wording they haven't seen and can't reason out. It isn't a word that carries the meaning.

findings.problem: Cards 18 and 19 already asked about Genesis 21:33 and 21:34. Card 20 retells both ("calls on the LORD... settles in for a long stay"), so it works as a recap. Since the last verse was asked on a choice card, this card should be only the line saying the story isn't over.
The line saying the story isn't over ("That's where we leave him for now, friend, but trust me...") nearly copies the example line in the doc. It should be a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin is mostly flat across the walkthrough. Only cards 1, 10 and 12 try for a laugh. Cards 3 and 16, and the well dispute in cards 7 and 8, read like a nice dad being pleasant, even though these moments could hold a real laugh without muddying a fact.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend.
